title: Pilot surge lane cookbook and draft release notes (May 2027)
content:
Context

Purpose: compact cookbook for running a small, fast-turn pilot surge lane (target: 48–72 hours) to validate behavior for performance-sensitive changes (routing, batching, quantization profile swap). This doc combines operator checklists, a 3-day rollout calendar, smoke telemetry probes, and a draft of the release notes for customer-facing comms.

When to use this lane
- Low-risk config/model change that impacts latency/costs, but could have systemic tail effects.
- Need fast feedback from production for a tight experiment window.
- Timeboxed trial where we want aggressive telemetry sampling and short rollback/rollforward cycles.

High-level phases (3-phase, ~72h max)
1) Preflight (0.5–4h) — verify readiness, lock freeze window, run local staging smoke tests.
2) Micro-canary (6–12h) — route 0.5–2% traffic in 1–3 micro-canaries across regions. Tight telemetry hooks.
3) Surge ramp (remainder up to 72h) — gradual ramp (2% -> 10% -> 30%), continue sampling and run full regression suites.

Operator checklist (preflight) — owner: release lead
- Confirm preflight owner and primary/backup on-call (Slack ping: #releases).
- Post preflight note to #releases with kickoff ETA and JIRA links.
- Validate model/artifact build hash and manifest; confirm pinned model version in config.
- Run staging end-to-end smoke: inference warmup (kv cache hit test), basic latencies at 95/99 percentiles, simple correctness check against golden prompts.
- Validate observability: dashboards live for route/model, trace sampling at 1000rps for first hour, alerts ready and tested (muting rules cleared).
- Confirm rollback playbook prepared and quick action commands tested (traffic switch, deploy previous artifact).
- Confirm billing/quotas are acceptable for burst (ops and finance informed).
- Mark preflight complete in JIRA and update the release calendar.

Micro-canary checklist — owner: canary steward
- Create micro-canary route(s) with 0.5–2% of traffic. Use two orthogonal splits (region A + region B) if possible.
- Start with a low request rate sample (5m warmup), then enable target load.
- Observe for 30–60m at each step: latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, queue depth, GPU utilization, OOMs.
- Run automated sample prompt set (100 unique prompts) every 15 minutes; compare to golden outputs and log diffs.
- Verify KV/prefix cache behavior: confirm expected cache hit ratio for common prefixes.
- Ensure fallback routes exist (auto-fallback to non-quantized model or older kernel build).
- If any of the following triggers, abort canary and execute rollback: error rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m, p99 increase > 2x baseline, OOM or repeated model failures, or output-quality regression with high confidence. Document trigger in JIRA.

Surge ramp checklist — owner: release conductor
- Ramp plan: 2% -> 10% -> 30% over 6–12h with observation windows (30–60m) between steps.
- For each ramp step validate: latency, error rate, GPU/tensor core utilization, tail latencies on long-sequence requests, and system-level alarms (network, infra).
- Gradual increase of trace sampling weight to capture variability.
- Start targeted synthetic traffic that simulates peak shapes for top 10 customers.
- Confirm canary readouts: model-level cost per token estimate, cumulative token spend relative to budget.
- Notify product and CS at 10% and 30% ramp points with short status update.
- If rollback criteria hit, pause ramp and run rollback checklist.

Rollback quick actions
- Immediate: flip traffic routing to previous compatible model/route (one-click route switchbook). Post status to #releases and call handoff.
- If route switch unavailable: deploy hotfix build with previous kernel selection and restart serving pods.
- Post-rollback: capture full traces for last 60m and tag as rollback event. Open postmortem ticket if rollback > 15m.

Observability and telemetry probes (what to watch)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 and distribution sketch for both short and long sequences.
- Errors: application-level exceptions, model load failures, RPC timeouts, retry storms.
- Resource: GPU mem/SM utilization, host load, PCIe transfer rates.
- Model correctness: automated sample set diffs (fuzzy similarity + token-level edit distance).
- Telemetry smoke probes: every 5m run 20 labeled probes that represent critical flows (embedding calls, chat flows, long sequence generation).
- Alerting: immediate P99 latency spike, error rate thresholds, sudden shift in similarity score distribution.

3-day rollout calendar (compact timeline)
Day 0 (pre-kickoff) — T-8h to T-0h
- Final staging smoke at T-8h, confirm data and manifests.
- Ops standby roster published.
- Slack announce: T-1h pre-kickoff checklist and link to runbook.
Day 1 (micro-canary) — T0 to T12h
- T0: enable micro-canary route (0.5%). Wait 30m.
- T+1h: expand to 1%. Run sample set.
- T+4h: run regression suite; if green, prepare surge ramp.
Day 2 (surge ramp) — T12h to T36h
- Ramp to 2% -> 10% across 6–12h with observation windows.
- Midday: product/CS check-in.
- Evening: expanded telemetry sampling, cost projection run.
Day 3 (monitor & finalize) — T36h to T72h
- If stable at 30% for 12h, prepare for wider roll or conversion to sustained route (requires ops approval).
- Draft customer-facing release notes and internal playbook update.
- Post-release retro and short postmortem if any anomaly recorded.

Draft release notes (customer-facing)
Title: Pilot surge lane: inference performance tuning (May 2027)
Summary: We performed a controlled pilot to validate performance and cost improvements from an updated inference configuration. The pilot was limited to a small percentage of traffic and focused on latency improvements and better batching behavior. No customer data was exposed and we observed no production correctness regressions for monitored prompt sets.
What changed:
- Swapped to updated kernel selection that improves token throughput for medium-length sequences.
- Enabled adaptive micro-batching for selected routes.
- Tuned KV cache warmup settings to reduce cold-start latencies.
Why this matters:
- Lower average CPU/GPU time per token for many conversational workloads, which should reduce cost and improve latency for interactive use-cases.
- We will roll improvements to more customers as confidence grows.
How we tested:
- Staging smoke, micro-canary validation, and ramped surge lane with aggressive telemetry sampling.
- Continuous checks against an internal golden prompt set.
Known limitations:
- Very long sequence workloads (>=4096 tokens) were not part of this pilot; we will run a separate validation for long-form generation.
- Enterprise dedicated deployments will receive a scheduling note before any automatic model/quantization changes.

Notes to operators / loose items
- Need to formalize the cost bucketing for pilot events (ops + finance).
- Consider adding a lightweight integrity check that runs in the cold path to detect kernel regressions earlier.
- Follow-up: schedule a 1-hour retro within 72h post-pilot and capture actionable changes to rollout playbooks.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Canary route toggle: ops console -> routes -> pilot-surge -> split edit.
- Rollback command (kubectl alias): kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/infer-serving --selector=release=previous
- Relevant Jira: JIRA-REL-3142 (pilot config), JIRA-REL-3199 (canary instrumentation).
- Slack channel: #releases (announce), #infra-ops (infra alerts), #cs-notify (customer check-ins).

Unresolved questions (to discuss in retro)
- What's the minimal telemetry set that provides high confidence for quality regressions without incurring high cost?
- How should we automate go/no-go decisions vs. manual human approvals?

-- end of draft --
